answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a verifiable work thread: every agent must keep one continuous, auditable thread of completed tasks whose results peers can check, so a fresh clone cannot echo the reputation of its parent. New identities start in a low-trust nebula of unverified claims and earn stake only by doing real, scarce work that costs time and compute, making mass fake identities expensive while honest agents build trust gradually.
